"""Explicit construction of the symmetry group of a disconnected 1-type,
and a numerical check of the exact sequence

    1 -> prod_i Out(pi_1 C_i) -> hAut(| |_i C_i) -> Sym'(pi_0) -> 1 .

We build hAut as an explicit finite group of matrix normal forms <sigma, P>:
sigma is a permutation of the components and P_i is an element of
Out(pi_1 C_i) = Aut(Z/n) = (Z/n)^x for the cyclic examples used here, subject to
the constraint that sigma may only move a component to one of the same homotopy
type.  We then verify, by exhaustive enumeration:

  * the composition law makes this a group of the predicted order;
  * the map to permutations of the components is a homomorphism;
  * its kernel is exactly the product of the Out groups;
  * |kernel| * |image| = |hAut|  (exactness / first isomorphism theorem);
  * for a constant family the extension splits (the pure relabellings form a
    complementary subgroup), giving the wreath product.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations, product
from math import factorial, gcd
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

# A component is described by the modulus n of its fundamental group Z/n
# (n = 1 gives a point).  Out(Z/n) = (Z/n)^x, of order phi(n).
Element = Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]  # (sigma as a tuple, units P)


def units(n: int) -> List[int]:
    return [u for u in range(1, n + 1) if gcd(u, n) == 1] if n > 1 else [1]


def allowed_permutations(mods: Sequence[int]) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Permutations of the components preserving the homotopy type of each."""
    k = len(mods)
    return [p for p in permutations(range(k)) if all(mods[i] == mods[p[i]] for i in range(k))]


def group_elements(mods: Sequence[int]) -> List[Element]:
    perms = allowed_permutations(mods)
    unit_choices = [units(m) for m in mods]
    return [(p, u) for p in perms for u in product(*unit_choices)]


def multiply(mods: Sequence[int], x: Element, y: Element) -> Element:
    """<sigma,P> . <tau,Q> = <sigma o tau, i |-> Q_i then P_{tau(i)}>."""
    (sigma, P), (tau, Q) = x, y
    k = len(mods)
    comp_perm = tuple(sigma[tau[i]] for i in range(k))
    comp_units = tuple((Q[i] * P[tau[i]]) % mods[i] if mods[i] > 1 else 1 for i in range(k))
    return (comp_perm, comp_units)


def check(mods: Sequence[int], name: str) -> None:
    els = group_elements(mods)
    k = len(mods)
    identity: Element = (tuple(range(k)), tuple(1 % m if m > 1 else 1 for m in mods))

    # closure, identity, inverses
    index = {e: i for i, e in enumerate(els)}
    for x in els:
        assert multiply(mods, x, identity) == x and multiply(mods, identity, x) == x
        assert any(multiply(mods, x, y) == identity for y in els)
        for y in els:
            assert multiply(mods, x, y) in index
    # associativity (sampled exhaustively for these small groups)
    for x in els:
        for y in els:
            for z in els:
                assert multiply(mods, multiply(mods, x, y), z) == \
                       multiply(mods, x, multiply(mods, y, z))

    kernel = [e for e in els if e[0] == tuple(range(k))]
    image = {e[0] for e in els}
    internal = 1
    for m in mods:
        internal *= len(units(m))
    multiplicities: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for m in mods:
        multiplicities[m] = multiplicities.get(m, 0) + 1
    external = 1
    for c in multiplicities.values():
        external *= factorial(c)

    assert len(kernel) == internal, (len(kernel), internal)
    assert len(image) == external, (len(image), external)
    assert len(els) == len(kernel) * len(image)

    # splitting for a constant family: pure relabellings form a subgroup
    split_ok = None
    if len(set(mods)) == 1:
        relabels = [(p, tuple(1 % m if m > 1 else 1 for m in mods))
                    for p in allowed_permutations(mods)]
        split_ok = all(multiply(mods, a, b) in relabels for a in relabels for b in relabels)

    print(f"{name}")
    print(f"    components (pi_1 = Z/n for n in) : {list(mods)}")
    print(f"    prod |Out|                        : {internal}")
    print(f"    |Sym'(pi_0)|                      : {external}")
    print(f"    |hAut| (enumerated)               : {len(els)}")
    print(f"    kernel x image = |hAut|           : {len(kernel)} x {len(image)} = {len(els)}  OK")
    if split_ok is not None:
        print(f"    extension splits (wreath product) : {split_ok}")
    print()


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    check([5, 5], "two copies of K(Z/5,1)   -- constant family, wreath product (Z/5)^x wr S_2")
    check([3, 5], "K(Z/3,1) u K(Z/5,1)      -- different homotopy types, no relabelling")
    check([1, 1, 1], "three points             -- all symmetry is combinatorial")
    check([7, 7, 3], "two copies of K(Z/7,1) and one K(Z/3,1)  -- mixed")
    print("All structural checks passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: Exhaustive Determination of the Outer Automorphism Order of a Finite Group
algorithms.description: Computes |Out(G)| for a finite group given by its multiplication table, which by the symmetry theorem is exactly the number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences of the aspherical space K(G,1). The algorithm first extracts a small generating set greedily; an endomorphism is then determined by the images of the generators, and only elements of the same order are admissible images of a given generator. Each candidate assignment is closed up multiplicatively, rejecting inconsistent or non-total closures, and the surviving maps are tested for bijectivity and the homomorphism property. Finally |Inn(G)| = |G|/|Z(G)| by the first isomorphism theorem applied to the conjugation map, and |Out(G)| = |Aut(G)|/|Inn(G)|. With generator pruning the cost is O(|G|^{d+1}) for a generating set of size d, plus O(|G|^2) per verified candidate; for the groups arising in practice (d <= 2 or 3) this is a few milliseconds.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT: multiplication table T of a finite group G on {0..n-1}, identity 0
OUTPUT: |Out(G)|

1. gens <- greedy generating set:
     gens <- []; S <- {0}
     for a in 1..n-1:
         if a in S: continue
         append a to gens; S <- closure of S union {a} under T
         if |S| = n: break
2. ord[a] <- least k >= 1 with a^k = 0, for all a
3. count <- 0
4. for each tuple (b_1..b_d) with ord[b_j] = ord[gens_j]:
     phi <- {0 -> 0, gens_j -> b_j}
     repeat until stable:
         for all (a, x), (b, y) in phi:
             if a*b in dom(phi) and phi[a*b] != x*y: reject
             else phi[a*b] <- x*y
     if dom(phi) != G: reject
     if phi is not injective: reject
     if exists a,b with phi[a*b] != phi[a]*phi[b]: reject
     count <- count + 1
5. Z <- { z : z*a = a*z for all a };  inn <- n / |Z|
6. return count / inn

algorithms.name: Order Formula for the Symmetry Group of an Arbitrary Homotopy 1-Type
algorithms.description: Given a homotopy 1-type presented as a finite disjoint union of connected aspherical components, each labelled by the isomorphism type of its fundamental group together with |Out| and |Z| of that group, this routine returns the orders of all three groups in the exact sequence of the structure theorem. Two components have the same homotopy type exactly when their fundamental groups are isomorphic, so partitioning by the isomorphism label yields multiplicities m_1,...,m_r and |Sym'(pi_0)| = prod_k m_k!. The internal contribution is prod_i |Out(pi_1 C_i)|, the total is their product, and the group of self-homotopies of the identity has order prod_i |Z(pi_1 C_i)|. Infinite values are propagated as None. The cost is linear in the number of components once the outer automorphism orders are known, so the whole computation is dominated by the group-theoretic preprocessing of the previous algorithm.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT: components C_1..C_n, each with (iso_key, |Out|, |Z|)
OUTPUT: (internal, external, total, higher)

1. multiplicities <- empty map
2. for each component C:
     multiplicities[C.iso_key] <- multiplicities[C.iso_key] + 1
3. external <- product over k of factorial(multiplicities[k])
     (this is |Sym'(pi_0)|: only look-alike components may be permuted)
4. internal <- product over i of |Out(pi_1 C_i)|   (infinite if any factor is)
5. higher   <- product over i of |Z(pi_1 C_i)|     (infinite if any factor is)
6. total    <- internal * external                 (infinite if internal is)
7. return (internal, external, total, higher)
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm B: order of the symmetry group of an arbitrary homotopy 1-type.

Input: the list of connected components, each described by the isomorphism type
of its fundamental group together with |Out| and |Z| of that group (None for an
infinite value).  Output: the orders of the three groups in the exact sequence

    1 -> prod_i Out(pi_1 C_i) -> hAut(| |_i C_i) -> Sym'(pi_0) -> 1

together with the order of the group of self-homotopies of the identity,
prod_i |Z(pi_1 C_i)|.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from math import factorial
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Piece:
    """One connected aspherical component of a 1-type."""

    label: str
    iso_key: str              # isomorphism type of pi_1 == homotopy type of the piece
    out_order: Optional[int]  # |Out(pi_1)|, None if infinite
    centre_order: Optional[int]  # |Z(pi_1)|, None if infinite


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SymmetryReport:
    internal: Optional[int]   # prod_i |Out(pi_1 C_i)|
    external: int             # |Sym'(pi_0)| = prod_k m_k!
    total: Optional[int]      # |hAut|
    higher: Optional[int]     # |Aut(identity)| = prod_i |Z(pi_1 C_i)|
    multiplicities: Dict[str, int]


def symmetry_report(pieces: Sequence[Piece]) -> SymmetryReport:
    multiplicities: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for p in pieces:
        multiplicities[p.iso_key] = multiplicities.get(p.iso_key, 0) + 1

    external = 1
    for m in multiplicities.values():
        external *= factorial(m)

    internal: Optional[int] = 1
    for p in pieces:
        if p.out_order is None or internal is None:
            internal = None
        else:
            internal *= p.out_order

    higher: Optional[int] = 1
    for p in pieces:
        if p.centre_order is None or higher is None:
            higher = None
        else:
            higher *= p.centre_order

    total = None if internal is None else internal * external
    return SymmetryReport(internal, external, total, higher, multiplicities)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    circle = Piece("K(Z,1)", "Z", 2, None)
    lens3 = Piece("K(Z/3,1)", "Z/3", 2, 3)
    s3 = Piece("K(S_3,1)", "S_3", 1, 1)
    klein = Piece("K(V,1)", "V", 6, 4)

    for name, pieces in [
        ("K(Z,1) u K(Z/3,1)", [circle, lens3]),
        ("three copies of K(S_3,1)", [s3, s3, s3]),
        ("two copies of K(V,1)", [klein, klein]),
    ]:
        r = symmetry_report(pieces)
        print(f"{name}: #hAut = {r.total}  (internal {r.internal} x external {r.external})")

algorithms.name: Matrix Normal Form and Composition of Self-Maps of a Disjoint Union
algorithms.description: Implements the normal-form theorem computationally. A homotopy class of self-maps of a disjoint union of connected aspherical components is stored as a pair: an index map sigma on the components, and for each i an entry recording the homotopy class of the induced map from the i-th component to the sigma(i)-th. Composition is the matrix rule: the index maps compose and the entries multiply along the path, so composing costs O(n) entry-compositions. Invertibility -- equivalently, being a homotopy equivalence -- is decided by testing that the index map is a bijection and that every entry is invertible, again in O(n). The entry type is a parameter: for unions of circles the entries are integer degrees and composition is multiplication, while in general they are conjugacy classes of homomorphisms of fundamental groups. A display routine renders a normal form as the sparse matrix with a single nonzero entry per column.
algorithms.pseudocode:
REPRESENTATION: a self-map is <sigma, P> with sigma : {0..n-1} -> {0..n-1}
                and P[i] a homotopy class of maps C_i -> C_{sigma(i)}

COMPOSE(f = <sigma,P>, g = <tau,Q>):        # f after g
  1. for i in 0..n-1:
  2.     index[i] <- sigma[tau[i]]
  3.     entry[i] <- P[tau[i]] composed after Q[i]
  4. return <index, entry>

IDENTITY(n): return <i |-> i, all entries the identity class>

IS_EQUIVALENCE(f = <sigma,P>):
  1. if sigma is not a bijection: return false
  2. if some P[i] is not invertible: return false
  3. return true

TO_MATRIX(f = <sigma,P>): matrix M with M[sigma[i]][i] = P[i], else 0
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm C: the matrix normal form of a self-map of a disjoint union.

A homotopy class of self-maps of a disjoint union of connected aspherical
pieces is a pair <sigma, P>: an index map sigma on the components together
with, for each i, a homotopy class of maps C_i -> C_{sigma(i)}.  Composition is
matrix multiplication:

    <sigma,P> . <tau,Q> = <sigma o tau, i |-> Q_i then P_{tau(i)}> ,

and the class is invertible -- i.e. the map is a homotopy equivalence -- exactly
when sigma is a bijection and every entry is invertible.

Here the entries are modelled concretely: for a union of circles an entry is an
integer (the degree), and the composition rule specialises to multiplication of
degrees.  The same code works for any entry type with a composition operation
and a notion of invertibility.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, Generic, List, Sequence, TypeVar

E = TypeVar("E")  # type of an entry: a homotopy class of maps between two pieces


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SelfMap(Generic[E]):
    """<sigma, P> in matrix normal form on n components."""

    index_map: Sequence[int]  # sigma: {0..n-1} -> {0..n-1}
    entries: Sequence[E]      # entries[i] is the class of the map C_i -> C_{sigma(i)}

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        return len(self.index_map)


def compose(f: SelfMap[E], g: SelfMap[E],
            entry_compose: Callable[[E, E], E]) -> SelfMap[E]:
    """f after g, i.e. <sigma,P> . <tau,Q>."""
    n = g.size
    assert f.size == n, "both self-maps must act on the same number of components"
    index_map: List[int] = [f.index_map[g.index_map[i]] for i in range(n)]
    entries: List[E] = [
        entry_compose(f.entries[g.index_map[i]], g.entries[i]) for i in range(n)
    ]
    return SelfMap(index_map, entries)


def identity(n: int, unit: E) -> SelfMap[E]:
    return SelfMap(list(range(n)), [unit] * n)


def is_equivalence(f: SelfMap[E], entry_invertible: Callable[[E], bool]) -> bool:
    """Invertible iff the index map is a bijection and every entry is invertible."""
    return (len(set(f.index_map)) == f.size
            and all(entry_invertible(e) for e in f.entries))


def to_matrix(f: SelfMap[int], zero: int = 0) -> List[List[int]]:
    """Display form: the (sigma(i), i) entry is the i-th class, all others zero."""
    n = f.size
    m = [[zero] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        m[f.index_map[i]][i] = f.entries[i]
    return m


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Three circles.  Entries are degrees; composition multiplies them.
    deg_compose = lambda a, b: a * b
    deg_invertible = lambda a: a in (1, -1)

    f: SelfMap[int] = SelfMap([1, 2, 0], [1, -1, 1])      # cyclic shift, degrees +-1
    g: SelfMap[int] = SelfMap([0, 1, 2], [2, 1, -3])      # fixes components, degree 2 and -3

    for name, m in [("f", f), ("g", g), ("f o g", compose(f, g, deg_compose))]:
        print(name, "matrix:", to_matrix(m),
              "equivalence:", is_equivalence(m, deg_invertible))

visualizations.name: Symmetries of the Infinite Lens Space are Euler's Totient
visualizations.description: Plots, for n up to 120, the number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences of the infinite lens space K(Z/n,1), which the totient theorem identifies with phi(n). Prime n, where the count attains its maximum n-1, are circled, and the bound n-1 is drawn for reference; the lower panel shows the density phi(n)/n, making visible that the count oscillates for purely arithmetic reasons -- it depends on how many small primes divide n, something invisible to any dimension or continuity argument.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: the symmetry count of the lens space K(Z/n,1) is phi(n).

Plots, for 1 <= n <= 120, the number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy-
equivalences of the infinite lens space K(Z/n,1).  By the totient theorem this
number equals Euler's totient phi(n), so the plot is simultaneously a picture of
a homotopy invariant and of an arithmetic function.  Prime n (where the count is
exactly n-1, the maximum possible) are highlighted, and the line n-1 is drawn
for reference.  The lower panel shows the density phi(n)/n, making visible that
the symmetry count oscillates for arithmetic reasons.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from math import gcd
from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def euler_totient(n: int) -> int:
    return sum(1 for k in range(1, n + 1) if gcd(k, n) == 1)


def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    if n < 2:
        return False
    d = 2
    while d * d <= n:
        if n % d == 0:
            return False
        d += 1
    return True


def main(nmax: int = 120) -> None:
    ns: List[int] = list(range(1, nmax + 1))
    vals: List[int] = [euler_totient(n) for n in ns]
    primes: List[int] = [n for n in ns if is_prime(n)]
    prime_vals: List[int] = [euler_totient(n) for n in primes]

    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(11, 8),
                                   gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})

    ax1.plot(ns, [n - 1 for n in ns], color="lightgray", lw=1,
             label="upper bound $n-1$")
    ax1.vlines(ns, 0, vals, color="#4c72b0", alpha=0.35, lw=1)
    ax1.scatter(ns, vals, s=14, color="#4c72b0",
                label=r"$\#\,\mathrm{hAut}(K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1))$")
    ax1.scatter(primes, prime_vals, s=42, facecolor="none", edgecolor="#c44e52",
                lw=1.4, label="prime $n$ (count $= n-1$)")
    ax1.set_xlabel("$n$")
    ax1.set_ylabel("homotopy classes of self-equivalences")
    ax1.set_title("Symmetries of the infinite lens space $K(\\mathbb{Z}/n,1)$ "
                  "equal Euler's totient $\\varphi(n)$")
    ax1.legend(loc="upper left")
    ax1.grid(alpha=0.25)

    ax2.scatter(ns, [v / n for v, n in zip(vals, ns)], s=14, color="#55a868")
    ax2.axhline(1.0, color="lightgray", lw=1)
    ax2.set_xlabel("$n$")
    ax2.set_ylabel(r"$\varphi(n)/n$")
    ax2.set_title("Density of symmetries: the oscillation is arithmetic, not topological")
    ax2.grid(alpha=0.25)

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("lens_space_symmetries.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote lens_space_symmetries.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: The Two Sources of Symmetry in a Disconnected Space
visualizations.description: Illustrates the exact sequence of the structure theorem by factoring the order of the symmetry group into its internal part (the product of the outer automorphism groups of the pieces) and its external part (relabellings of look-alike pieces). The left panel plots, on a logarithmic scale, the wreath-product growth |Out(G)|^n n! for n copies of K(G,1) for several G, against the pure-relabelling curve n!; the right panel contrasts concrete two- and three-piece spaces, showing that a space can be dominated by either source -- three copies of the rigid space K(S_3,1) have only relabelling symmetry, while a circle next to a lens space has only internal symmetry.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: the two sources of symmetry in a disconnected 1-type.

For a disjoint union of connected aspherical pieces the symmetry group sits in
the exact sequence

    1 -> prod_i Out(pi_1 C_i) -> hAut -> Sym'(pi_0) -> 1,

so its order factors as an "internal" part (outer automorphisms of the pieces)
times an "external" part (relabellings of look-alike pieces).  The left panel
shows this factorisation, on a logarithmic scale, for n copies of K(G,1) with
several choices of G; the right panel contrasts three concrete two- and
three-piece spaces, showing how a space can be dominated by either source.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from math import factorial
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def constant_family_order(out_order: int, n: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """(internal, external) contributions for n copies of one K(G,1)."""
    return out_order ** n, factorial(n)


def main() -> None:
    families: Dict[str, int] = {
        "$K(S_3,1)$  ($|\\mathrm{Out}|=1$)": 1,
        "$K(\\mathbb{Z},1)$  ($|\\mathrm{Out}|=2$)": 2,
        "$K(\\mathbb{Z}/5,1)$  ($|\\mathrm{Out}|=4$)": 4,
        "$K(V,1)$  ($|\\mathrm{Out}|=6$)": 6,
    }
    ns: List[int] = list(range(1, 9))

    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))

    for label, o in families.items():
        totals = [constant_family_order(o, n)[0] * factorial(n) for n in ns]
        ax1.semilogy(ns, totals, marker="o", label=label)
    ax1.semilogy(ns, [factorial(n) for n in ns], color="gray", ls="--",
                 label="pure relabelling $n!$")
    ax1.set_xlabel("number $n$ of copies")
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"$\#\,\mathrm{hAut} = |\mathrm{Out}(G)|^n\, n!$")
    ax1.set_title("Constant families: the wreath product "
                  r"$\mathrm{Out}(G)\wr\mathrm{Sym}(n)$")
    ax1.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax1.grid(alpha=0.25, which="both")

    examples: List[Tuple[str, int, int]] = [
        (r"$K(\mathbb{Z},1)\sqcup K(\mathbb{Z}/3,1)$", 4, 1),
        (r"$K(\mathbb{Z},1)\sqcup K(\mathbb{Z},1)$", 4, 2),
        (r"$3\times K(S_3,1)$", 1, 6),
        (r"$2\times K(V,1)$", 36, 2),
        (r"$K(\mathbb{Z}/3,1)\sqcup 2\times K(\mathbb{Z}/5,1)$", 32, 2),
    ]
    idx = np.arange(len(examples))
    internal = np.array([e[1] for e in examples], dtype=float)
    external = np.array([e[2] for e in examples], dtype=float)
    ax2.bar(idx, internal, label=r"internal: $\prod_i|\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1C_i)|$",
            color="#4c72b0")
    ax2.bar(idx, external, bottom=internal,
            label=r"external: $|\mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0)|$", color="#dd8452")
    for k, (name, i_val, e_val) in enumerate(examples):
        ax2.text(k, i_val + e_val + 1.2, f"$\\#\\mathrm{{hAut}}={i_val*e_val}$",
                 ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax2.set_xticks(idx)
    ax2.set_xticklabels([e[0] for e in examples], rotation=18, fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_ylabel("order of the contribution")
    ax2.set_title("Two sources of symmetry (heights added, orders multiplied)")
    ax2.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax2.grid(alpha=0.25, axis="y")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("symmetry_sources.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote symmetry_sources.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_demos.title: The Symmetry Calculator for Aspherical Spaces
interactive_demos.description: Build a homotopy 1-type piece by piece from a palette of aspherical spaces -- the circle, tori, lens spaces K(Z/n,1) for any n you type, the rigid space K(S_3,1), the Klein-four space, K(Q_8,1), K(D_4,1), a figure eight, a point -- and read off, exactly, the number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences of the resulting space. The widget displays the exact sequence of the structure theorem with each of its terms evaluated: the internal contribution (the product of the outer automorphism groups of the pieces), the external contribution (the type-preserving permutations of the components, computed from the multiplicities of the homotopy types), the total, and the order of the group of self-homotopies of the identity. A diagram draws the pieces with their internal symmetry counts and joins interchangeable pieces by dashed arcs, so it is immediately visible which pieces a symmetry is allowed to move. Two progressive-disclosure panels explain why the answer is Out(G) rather than Aut(G), and why only look-alike pieces can be swapped.

Why is the answer Out(G) and not Aut(G)? (click to reveal)

A self-map of a connected aspherical space is determined up to homotopy by the homomorphism it induces on the fundamental group — but only up to conjugacy, because nothing pins down where the basepoint goes. Dragging the basepoint once around a loop a changes the induced homomorphism by conjugation by a. So inner automorphisms act trivially on homotopy classes, and the symmetry group is Aut(G)/Inn(G) = Out(G).

The automorphisms that disappear are not lost: they reappear one level up. The self-homotopies of the identity map form the centre Z(G), which is exactly the kernel of G → Inn(G). Symmetry of a space is a two-layer structure, and its two layers are the cokernel and the kernel of G → Aut(G).

Why can only look-alike pieces be swapped? (click to reveal)

A map out of a connected space has connected image, so it lands inside a single component of the target. Hence a self-map of a disjoint union is exactly a rule σ saying which piece goes to which, plus one homotopy class of maps Cᵢ → Cσ(i) for each i — a matrix with one entry per column. If the self-map is invertible, each of those entries is an equivalence, so Cᵢ and Cσ(i) must have the same homotopy type; and conversely any type-preserving permutation is realised by assembling chosen equivalences. Since a connected aspherical space is determined by its fundamental group, "same homotopy type" simply means "isomorphic fundamental group".

interactive_demos.title: The Matrix Normal Form: Composing Self-Maps of a Union of Circles
interactive_demos.description: A hands-on illustration of the normal-form theorem. Choose the number of circles, then specify two self-maps by saying, for each circle, where it goes and with what degree. The widget renders each self-map as the sparse matrix with one entry per column, composes them by the matrix rule of the theorem -- index maps compose, degrees multiply along the path -- and reports for each of the three maps whether it is invertible, i.e. a homotopy equivalence, which happens exactly when the index map is a bijection and every degree is plus or minus one. This makes concrete both the classification of all self-maps (not only the equivalences) and the count 2^n n! of symmetries of a union of n circles.

The general rule (click to reveal)

For an arbitrary disjoint union ⊔i Ci of connected aspherical pieces, a homotopy class of self-maps is a pair ⟨σ, P⟩: an index map σ and, for each i, a homotopy class of maps Ci → Cσ(i). Composition is

⟨σ,P⟩ · ⟨τ,Q⟩ = ⟨σ∘τ, i ↦ Qi then Pτ(i)⟩
which is exactly matrix multiplication. For circles the entries are integers — the classical degree — because homotopy classes of maps between circles are classified by an integer and composition multiplies degrees. In general the entries are conjugacy classes of homomorphisms of fundamental groups.

The class is invertible — that is, the map is a homotopy equivalence — exactly when σ is a bijection and every entry is invertible. For circles that means every degree is ±1, so a union of n circles has 2n · n! symmetries.

# The Shape of a Group: symmetries of aspherical spaces *A guided tour. By the end of this page you will be able to look at a space built out of loops and say, exactly, how many symmetries it has — and you will know why the answer is a piece of group theory.* --- ## 1. The question Topology forgets almost everything. Stretch, bend, squash — but never tear or glue — and a coffee cup becomes a doughnut. What survives? The oldest survivor is the **fundamental group**. Fix a point $x$ in a space $X$; consider all loops based at $x$, where two loops are the same if one slides continuously into the other. Concatenation makes these classes a group $\pi_1(X,x)$. The circle gives $\pi_1(S^1)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ (count the windings); the torus gives $\mathbb{Z}^2$. On its own $\pi_1$ is a weak invariant: the sphere and a point both have trivial fundamental group. So we restrict to the class of spaces where it is *not* weak. > **Definition.** A **homotopy $1$-type** is a space all of whose higher homotopy groups $\pi_2,\pi_3,\dots$ vanish. A connected one with fundamental group $G$ is an **Eilenberg–MacLane space** $K(G,1)$, or an **aspherical** space. Every group is the fundamental group of such a space, and that space is unique up to deformation. Familiar examples: the circle is a $K(\mathbb{Z},1)$; the $n$-torus a $K(\mathbb{Z}^n,1)$; the infinite lens space a $K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)$; a bouquet of $k$ circles a $K(F_k,1)$ for the free group $F_k$; every closed surface of genus $\ge 1$ is aspherical.
The dictionary that makes everything computable (click to reveal) A homotopy $1$-type is the same thing as a **groupoid** — a category all of whose arrows are invertible. Given a space, take its points as objects and homotopy classes of paths as arrows. Then: | topology | groupoid | |---|---| | space | groupoid $C$ | | path components $\pi_0$ | isomorphism classes of objects | | $\pi_1(X,x)$ | the vertex group $\mathrm{Aut}(x)$ | | continuous map | functor | | homotopy | natural isomorphism | | homotopy equivalence | equivalence of categories | | $K(G,1)$ | connected groupoid with vertex group $G$ | The smallest model of $K(G,1)$ is the **one-object groupoid**: one object $\star$, with arrow set $G$. A group *is* a space, in this precise sense. Everything below is easiest to think about through this dictionary; see the [nLab entry on groupoids](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/groupoid) for more.
--- ## 2. The two foundational theorems > **Complete invariance.** Two connected $1$-types are homotopy equivalent **if and only if** their fundamental groups are isomorphic. > **Classification of maps.** For connected $1$-types, > $$[K(G,1),\,K(H,1)] \;\cong\; \mathrm{Hom}(G,H)/\text{conjugation}.$$ A map between aspherical spaces *is* a homomorphism of fundamental groups — up to conjugacy, because nothing pins down where the basepoint goes. Dragging the basepoint once around a loop $a$ changes the induced homomorphism by conjugation by $a$; that is a homotopy, not new information. This single formula is the engine of everything that follows. --- ## 3. Symmetries of a connected aspherical space Composition makes the homotopy classes of self-maps of a space $X$ into a **monoid** $[X,X]$; inside it sits the group $\mathrm{hAut}(X)$ of invertible classes, the homotopy self-equivalences. > **Monoid classification.** For a connected $1$-type with $\pi_1 = G$, the monoid $[X,X]$ is the monoid of **conjugacy classes of endomorphisms** of $G$. > **Invertibility.** A class in $[X,X]$ is invertible exactly when it is represented by a homotopy equivalence. > **The symmetry theorem.** $\mathrm{hAut}(K(G,1)) \cong \mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G)/\mathrm{Inn}(G)$. > **One level up.** The self-homotopies of the identity map form the centre $Z(G)$. So the whole two-layer symmetry structure of an aspherical space is $(\mathrm{Out}\,G,\;Z(G))$ — the cokernel and the kernel of the map $G\to\mathrm{Aut}(G)$, $a\mapsto(g\mapsto aga^{-1})$.
Proof sketch of the symmetry theorem (click to reveal) By the classification of maps, $[X,X]\cong\mathrm{End}(G)/\text{conj}$, and one checks this respects composition, so it is an isomorphism of monoids. Now take units. If the class of $\phi$ is invertible, composing with a representative $\psi$ of the inverse class gives $\psi\phi = c_a$, an inner automorphism, which is bijective; hence $\phi$ is injective and surjective, i.e. an automorphism. Conversely automorphisms are clearly invertible. Finally, two automorphisms are conjugate exactly when they differ by an inner automorphism, so the unit group is $\mathrm{Aut}(G)/\mathrm{Inn}(G)=\mathrm{Out}(G)$. $\blacksquare$ For the higher layer: a self-homotopy of the identity assigns to each point $x$ a loop $\alpha_x$, and naturality forces $\alpha_x$ to commute with everything in $\pi_1(X,x)$, i.e. to be central; connectedness makes $\alpha$ determined by $\alpha_{x_0}$, and every central element occurs. $\blacksquare$
--- ## 4. Compute it yourself Here is the theory as a calculator. Add pieces to a space and read off, exactly, how many symmetries it has. Start with a single piece to see the connected theory in action; then add a second identical piece and watch a new source of symmetry appear. {{interactive_demo:0}} Things to try: * **$K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)$ for various $n$.** The count is $\varphi(n)$, Euler's totient — it leaps from $8$ at $n=30$ to $30$ at $n=31$. * **$K(S_3,1)$.** A nonabelian fundamental group of order $6$, and yet exactly **one** symmetry: the space is completely rigid, because every automorphism of $S_3$ is inner. * **$K(V,1)$ for the Klein four group.** An abelian fundamental group whose symmetry group $\mathrm{Aut}(V)\cong S_3$ is *nonabelian*. * **Two copies of the same piece versus two different pieces.** Watch the dashed arcs appear and the count jump by a factor of $2$. --- ## 5. Euler's totient, from topology The lens space computation deserves its own picture. Because $\mathbb{Z}/n$ is abelian, $\mathrm{Out} = \mathrm{Aut}$, and an automorphism of $\mathbb{Z}/n$ is multiplication by a unit: $$\mathrm{hAut}\bigl(K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)\bigr)\;\cong\;(\mathbb{Z}/n)^{\times},\qquad \#\,\mathrm{hAut}\bigl(K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)\bigr)\;=\;\varphi(n).$$ A question about rubber shapes, answered by the most elementary function in number theory. For $n=1,2$ the space is rigid; for prime $p$ the count is $p-1$, the largest it can be. {{visualization:0}} The oscillation in the lower panel is *arithmetic*: it depends on how many small prime factors $n$ has, something no dimension count or continuity argument could ever see. --- ## 6. Breaking the space into pieces Every $1$-type is the disjoint union of its connected components, so to finish the theory we must handle disconnected spaces. Here is the key observation, and it is almost obvious once said: > A map out of a **connected** space has connected image, so it lands inside a **single** component of the target. Therefore a self-map of $\bigsqcup_i C_i$ is exactly: 1. a rule $\sigma$ saying which component each component is sent to, and 2. for each $i$, a homotopy class of maps $C_i \to C_{\sigma(i)}$. That is a **matrix** with one nonzero entry per column, and composition is matrix multiplication: $$\langle\sigma,P\rangle\cdot\langle\tau,Q\rangle \;=\; \bigl\langle\, \sigma\circ\tau,\; i\mapsto Q_i\ \text{then}\ P_{\tau(i)} \,\bigr\rangle .$$ For a union of circles the entries are integers — the classical degree — and you can play with the multiplication directly: {{interactive_demo:1}} Notice what invertibility requires: the index map must be a bijection **and** every entry must be invertible. For circles that means all degrees are $\pm1$, so a union of $n$ circles has exactly $2^n\cdot n!$ symmetries. --- ## 7. The structure theorem Restricting the matrix description to invertible elements gives the final answer for an arbitrary $1$-type. > **Structure theorem.** For any family $(C_i)$ of connected $1$-types the sequence > $$1 \longrightarrow \prod_i \mathrm{Out}(\pi_1 C_i) \longrightarrow \mathrm{hAut}\Bigl(\bigsqcup_i C_i\Bigr) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0) \longrightarrow 1$$ > is exact, where $\mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0)$ is the group of permutations $\sigma$ of the components with $C_i \simeq C_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i$. The self-homotopies of the identity form $\prod_i Z(\pi_1 C_i)$. In one sentence: **a symmetry of a space is a shuffle of look-alike pieces followed by an internal symmetry of each piece — and nothing else.**
Why the image is exactly the type-preserving permutations (click to reveal) If a self-equivalence sends component $i$ to component $\sigma(i)$, then restricted to those components it is itself an equivalence, so $C_i\simeq C_{\sigma(i)}$. Conversely, given a permutation $\sigma$ with $C_i\simeq C_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i$, choose an equivalence $E_i : C_i \to C_{\sigma(i)}$ for each $i$ and assemble them. Because $\sigma$ is a bijection, the assembled map is full, faithful and essentially surjective — an equivalence — and it induces $\sigma$ on components. $\blacksquare$ And the kernel? A self-equivalence inducing the identity permutation is a **diagonal** matrix; the inverse of a diagonal matrix is diagonal, so each diagonal entry is separately invertible, i.e. an element of $\mathrm{hAut}(C_i)=\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1C_i)$. $\blacksquare$
Two extremes fall out immediately: * **All pieces the same.** Every permutation is realised, the extension splits, and we get the **wreath product** $\mathrm{Out}(G)\wr\mathrm{Sym}(n)$, of order $|\mathrm{Out}(G)|^n\cdot n!$. * **No two pieces alike.** No permutation is realised and the answer is the plain product $\prod_i\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1C_i)$. For instance, the union of a circle and an infinite lens space with fundamental group $\mathbb{Z}/3$ has exactly $2\times 2 = 4$ symmetries, none of which moves a component — the pieces cannot be swapped because $\mathbb{Z}$ is infinite and $\mathbb{Z}/3$ is not. Three copies of the rigid space $K(S_3,1)$, on the other hand, have exactly $3! = 6$ symmetries, all of them pure relabelling. {{visualization:1}} --- ## 8. The algorithms Everything above is effective. Three routines suffice. {{algorithm:0}} {{algorithm:1}} {{algorithm:2}} --- ## 9. Numerical laboratory Run the whole theory end to end: the totient theorem checked against brute-force automorphism counts, symmetry groups of a zoo of aspherical spaces, the self-map monoid (not only the equivalences), disjoint unions, wreath growth, and matrix normal forms. {{demo:0}} And here is an independent, structural check: the symmetry group of a disconnected space is built explicitly as a finite group of matrix normal forms, and exactness of the sequence is verified by exhaustive enumeration. {{demo:1}} --- ## 10. Where this leads Aspherical spaces are the exact place where topology and group theory become one subject. That is why they are the home of some of the hardest open problems in the field — the [Borel conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borel_conjecture), the Farrell–Jones conjecture, and much of [geometric group theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_group_theory). What we have set out here is the homotopy-theoretic half of that program, in complete generality: which spaces are classified by their fundamental groups, how many symmetries they have, which symmetries mix which pieces, and what sits one level above. Natural next questions: when does the extension in the structure theorem fail to split? What is $\mathrm{Out}$ for a free group, or for a surface group (where it is the mapping class group, by the [Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehn%E2%80%93Nielsen%E2%80%93Baer_theorem))? And what replaces $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ one dimension up, where a space is described by $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$ as a module over it, and a cohomological $k$-invariant?

-- ===== FILE: Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupCyclicSelfEquivalences.lean =====
/-
# `K(ℤ/n,1)` has exactly `φ(n)` self-homotopy-equivalences

Using the main theorem of `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupOuterAutomorphisms.lean` — the
homotopy self-equivalence group of a `K(G,1)` is `Out G` — we compute this group for the
infinite family of cyclic fundamental groups.  Since a cyclic group is abelian, `Out` is
the full automorphism group, and `Aut(ℤ/n) ≅ (ℤ/n)ˣ`.  Hence

  `hAut(K(ℤ/n,1)) ≅ (ℤ/n)ˣ`  and  `#hAut(K(ℤ/n,1)) = φ(n)`

(`hEndUnitsCyclicMulEquivUnits`, `card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel`), a bridge between homotopy
theory and elementary number theory: the number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy
equivalences of the infinite lens-space-like `K(ℤ/n,1)` is Euler's totient of `n`.

We also record the additive/multiplicative dictionary `mulAutMultiplicativeMulEquivAddAut`
identifying `Aut(Multiplicative A)` with `Aut(A)` for an additive group `A`.
-/
import Mathlib
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupOuterAutomorphisms

open CategoryTheory
open FundamentalGroupOut

namespace FundamentalGroupCyclic

/-- Automorphisms of the multiplicative copy of an additive group are its additive
automorphisms. -/
def mulAutMultiplicativeMulEquivAddAut (A : Type*) [AddGroup A] :
    MulAut (Multiplicative A) ≃* AddAut A where
  toFun e := AddEquiv.toMultiplicative.symm e
  invFun e := AddEquiv.toMultiplicative e
  left_inv e := by simp
  right_inv e := by simp
  map_mul' e f := by ext a; rfl

/-- The algebraic model of `K(ℤ/n,1)`: the one-object groupoid of the cyclic group of
order `n`. -/
abbrev CyclicModel (n : ℕ) : Type := SingleObj (Multiplicative (ZMod n))

/-- **The homotopy self-equivalence group of `K(ℤ/n,1)` is the unit group `(ℤ/n)ˣ`.** -/
noncomputable def hEndUnitsCyclicMulEquivUnits (n : ℕ) :
    (HEnd (CyclicModel n))ˣ ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ :=
  ((hEndUnitsSingleObjMulEquivMulAut (Multiplicative (ZMod n))
      (fun x y => mul_comm x y)).trans
    (mulAutMultiplicativeMulEquivAddAut (ZMod n))).trans (ZMod.AddAutEquivUnits n)

/-- **`K(ℤ/n,1)` has exactly `φ(n)` homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences.** -/
theorem card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] :
    Nat.card ((HEnd (CyclicModel n))ˣ) = n.totient := by
  rw [Nat.card_congr (hEndUnitsCyclicMulEquivUnits n).toEquiv, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card,
    ZMod.card_units_eq_totient]

/-- `K(ℤ/1,1)` and `K(ℤ/2,1)` are homotopy rigid: their only self-homotopy-equivalence up
to homotopy is the identity. -/
theorem card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel_two : Nat.card ((HEnd (CyclicModel 2))ˣ) = 1 := by
  rw [card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel 2]
  decide

/-- `K(ℤ/5,1)` has four homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences. -/
theorem card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel_five : Nat.card ((HEnd (CyclicModel 5))ˣ) = 4 := by
  rw [card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel 5]
  decide

/-- For a prime `p`, `K(ℤ/p,1)` has exactly `p - 1` homotopy classes of
self-homotopy-equivalences. -/
theorem card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel_prime (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    Nat.card ((HEnd (CyclicModel p))ˣ) = p - 1 := by
  haveI : NeZero p := ⟨hp.ne_zero⟩
  rw [card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel p, Nat.totient_prime hp]

end FundamentalGroupCyclic

-- ===== FILE: Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupHeterogeneousExamples.lean =====
/-
# Two concrete disjoint unions: a rigid one and a symmetric one

`Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupHeterogeneousWreath.lean` computes the homotopy
self-equivalence group of an arbitrary disjoint union `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` of connected 1-types: it is
an extension of the group of permutations of the components preserving their homotopy type
by `∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ)`.  This file exhibits the two extreme behaviours of that extension on
concrete examples.

* `twoPieces` is the disjoint union `K(ℤ,1) ⊔ K(ℤ/3,1)` (a circle and an infinite lens
  space).  Its two components are **not** homotopy equivalent (`twoPieces_pairwise`), so no
  self-equivalence can interchange them (`twoPieces_perm_trivial`) and
  `card_hAut_twoPieces` : it has exactly `2 · 2 = 4` homotopy classes of
  self-homotopy-equivalences, namely `Out(ℤ) × Out(ℤ/3) = ±1 × (ℤ/3)ˣ`.
* For a *constant* family the opposite happens: `perm_surjective_of_constant` shows every
  permutation of the components is realised by a self-equivalence.
-/
import Mathlib
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupHeterogeneousWreath
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupCyclicSelfEquivalences

open CategoryTheory
open FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant (ConnectedAt)
open FundamentalGroupOut
open FundamentalGroupHetero

namespace FundamentalGroupHeteroExamples

/-! ## `K(ℤ,1) ⊔ K(ℤ/3,1)` -/

/-- The two-component 1-type `K(ℤ,1) ⊔ K(ℤ/3,1)`, as a family indexed by `Bool`. -/
def twoPieces : Bool → Type
  | false => CircleModel
  | true => FundamentalGroupCyclic.CyclicModel 3

instance instGroupoidTwoPieces : ∀ b, Groupoid (twoPieces b)
  | false => inferInstanceAs (Groupoid CircleModel)
  | true => inferInstanceAs (Groupoid (FundamentalGroupCyclic.CyclicModel 3))

/-- The chosen basepoints of the two components. -/
def twoBase : ∀ b, twoPieces b
  | false => SingleObj.star (Multiplicative ℤ)
  | true => SingleObj.star (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))

theorem twoPieces_connected : ∀ b, ConnectedAt (twoPieces b) (twoBase b)
  | false => singleObj_connected (Multiplicative ℤ)
  | true => singleObj_connected (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))

/-- The vertex group of the first component is `ℤ`. -/
noncomputable def twoAutFalse : Aut (twoBase false) ≃* Multiplicative ℤ :=
  singleObjAut (Multiplicative ℤ)

/-- The vertex group of the second component is `ℤ/3`. -/
noncomputable def twoAutTrue : Aut (twoBase true) ≃* Multiplicative (ZMod 3) :=
  singleObjAut (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))

/-- An equivalence between the two components would identify `ℤ` with `ℤ/3`. -/
theorem no_equivalence_false_true : ¬ Nonempty (twoPieces false ≌ twoPieces true) := by
  rintro ⟨E⟩
  obtain ⟨w⟩ := FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant.aut_mulEquiv_of_groupoid_equivalence E
    (twoBase false)
  have e : Multiplicative ℤ ≃ Multiplicative (ZMod 3) :=
    (twoAutFalse.symm.trans (w.trans twoAutTrue)).toEquiv
  haveI : Infinite (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)) := (Equiv.infinite_iff e).mp inferInstance
  exact not_finite (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))

/-- **The two components have different homotopy types.** -/
theorem twoPieces_pairwise (b b' : Bool) (h : Nonempty (twoPieces b ≌ twoPieces b')) :
    b = b' := by
  match b, b' with
  | false, false => rfl
  | true, true => rfl
  | false, true => exact absurd h no_equivalence_false_true
  | true, false =>
    exact absurd (h.map CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm) no_equivalence_false_true

/-- **No self-equivalence of `K(ℤ,1) ⊔ K(ℤ/3,1)` interchanges the two components.** -/
theorem twoPieces_perm_trivial (u : (HEnd (Σ b, twoPieces b))ˣ) :
    hAutSigmaToPerm twoPieces_connected u = 1 :=
  hAutSigmaToPerm_eq_one_of_pairwise twoPieces_connected twoPieces_pairwise u

theorem card_out_false : Nat.card (OutAut (Aut (twoBase false))) = 2 := by
  show Nat.card (OutAut (Aut (SingleObj.star (Multiplicative ℤ)))) = 2
  rw [← card_hEnd_units (C := CircleModel) (singleObj_connected (Multiplicative ℤ))]
  exact card_hEnd_units_circleModel

theorem card_out_true : Nat.card (OutAut (Aut (twoBase true))) = 2 := by
  show Nat.card (OutAut (Aut (SingleObj.star (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))))) = 2
  rw [← card_hEnd_units (C := FundamentalGroupCyclic.CyclicModel 3)
    (singleObj_connected (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)))]
  rw [FundamentalGroupCyclic.card_hEnd_units_cyclicModel 3]
  decide

/-- **`K(ℤ,1) ⊔ K(ℤ/3,1)` has exactly four homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences**
— the four pairs `(±1, ±1) ∈ Out(ℤ) × Out(ℤ/3)`, with no relabelling of the components. -/
theorem card_hAut_twoPieces : Nat.card ((HEnd (Σ b, twoPieces b))ˣ) = 4 := by
  rw [card_hAut_of_pairwise twoPieces_connected twoPieces_pairwise, Fintype.prod_bool,
    card_out_false, card_out_true]
  norm_num

/-! ## A constant family: every permutation of the components is realised -/

section Constant

universe w v u

variable {ι : Type w} {D : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} D] {d : D}

/-- **For a disjoint union of copies of one 1-type, every permutation of the components
comes from a self-homotopy-equivalence.**  This is the opposite extreme to
`twoPieces_perm_trivial`. -/
theorem perm_surjective_of_constant (hD : ConnectedAt D d) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
    ∃ u : (HEnd (Σ _ : ι, D))ˣ,
      hAutSigmaToPerm (C := fun _ : ι => D) (c := fun _ => d) (fun _ => hD) u = σ :=
  (exists_hAut_perm_iff (C := fun _ : ι => D) (c := fun _ => d) (fun _ => hD) σ).2
    fun _ => ⟨CategoryTheory.Equivalence.refl⟩

end Constant

end FundamentalGroupHeteroExamples

-- ===== FILE: Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupHeterogeneousWreath.lean =====
/-
# Self-maps of a disjoint union of *pairwise different* `K(G,1)`s

`Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupWreathProduct.lean` computes the monoid of homotopy
classes of self-maps, and the group of homotopy self-equivalences, of a disjoint union of
`ι` copies of **one** `K(G,1)`:

  `hAut (⊔_{i ∈ ι} K(G,1)) ≅ Out(G) ≀ Sym(ι)`.

This file removes the hypothesis that the components are all the same — item 1 of
`FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`.  For an arbitrary family `C : ι → Groupoid` of connected 1-types
(a general 1-type is the disjoint union of its components, see
`FundamentalGroupPi0Decomposition.lean`), the answer is a *matrix monoid*: a self-map of
`⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` is a self-map `σ` of the index set together with, for every `i`, a homotopy class
of maps `Cᵢ → C_{σ i}`.

* `HMap A B` : the set of homotopy classes of maps `A → B`, with composition `HMap.comp`;
* `WreathHom C` : the monoid of pairs `⟨σ, P⟩` with `σ : ι → ι` and
  `P i : HMap (C i) (C (σ i))`, multiplied by `⟨σ,P⟩ * ⟨τ,Q⟩ = ⟨σ ∘ τ, i ↦ Q i ; P (τ i)⟩`;
* `exists_factor` : a map out of a connected 1-type factors, up to homotopy, through a
  single component of the target — the technical heart;
* `hEndSigmaMulEquivWreath` : **`[⊔ᵢ Cᵢ, ⊔ᵢ Cᵢ] ≅ WreathHom C`** (all self-maps, not only
  the equivalences), and `wreathMulEquivHEndSigma` for the inverse isomorphism;
* `hAutSigmaToPerm` : the induced group homomorphism `hAut(⊔ᵢ Cᵢ) → Sym(ι)`, computed on
  representatives by `hAutSigmaToPerm_apply`;
* `exists_hAut_perm_iff` : its **image** consists exactly of the permutations `σ` with
  `Cᵢ ≌ C_{σ i}` for every `i`;
* `kerHAutSigmaToPermMulEquivPiOut` : its **kernel** is `∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ)` (via
  `diagUnitsMulEquivKer`, `kerMulEquivPiOut`).  So

    `1 → ∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ) → hAut(⊔ᵢ Cᵢ) → Sym'(π₀) → 1`

  is exact, where `Sym'` denotes the permutations of `π₀` preserving the homotopy type of
  each component;
* `hAutMulEquivPiOut_of_pairwise` : when no two components are homotopy equivalent, the
  answer is simply `∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ)`; `card_hAut_of_pairwise` counts it;
* `autIdSigmaMulEquivPiCenter` : the self-homotopies of the identity form `∏ᵢ Z(π₁ Cᵢ)`,
  so the whole automorphism 2-group of an arbitrary 1-type is determined.

Both extreme cases are recovered: for a constant family every permutation of the
components is realised (see `FundamentalGroupHeterogeneousExamples.perm_surjective_of_constant`
and, for the full wreath-product description, `FundamentalGroupWreathProduct.lean`), while
for pairwise inequivalent components none is.
-/
import Mathlib
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupOuterAutomorphisms
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupPi0Gluing
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupMapsClassification

open CategoryTheory
open FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant (ConnectedAt)
open FundamentalGroupK1
open FundamentalGroupOut

namespace FundamentalGroupHetero

universe w v u

/-! ## Homotopy classes of maps -/

section HMap

variable (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] (B : Type u) [Category.{v} B]

/-- Homotopy classes of maps of 1-types: natural-isomorphism classes of functors. -/
def HMap : Type max u v := Quotient (natIsoSetoid A B)

variable {A B}

/-- The homotopy class of a functor. -/
def HMap.mk (F : A ⥤ B) : HMap A B := Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid A B) F

theorem HMap.mk_eq_mk {F G : A ⥤ B} : HMap.mk F = HMap.mk G ↔ Nonempty (F ≅ G) :=
  Quotient.eq (r := natIsoSetoid A B)

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem HMap.ind {motive : HMap A B → Prop} (h : ∀ F : A ⥤ B, motive (HMap.mk F)) :
    ∀ q, motive q := Quotient.ind h

theorem HMap.mk_out (q : HMap A B) : HMap.mk (Quotient.out q) = q := Quotient.out_eq q

variable {E : Type u} [Category.{v} E]

/-- Composition of homotopy classes, in diagrammatic order. -/
def HMap.comp : HMap A B → HMap B E → HMap A E :=
  Quotient.map₂ (fun F G => F ⋙ G)
    (by
      rintro F F' ⟨eF⟩ G G' ⟨eG⟩
      exact ⟨(Functor.isoWhiskerRight eF G).trans (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft F' eG)⟩)

@[simp] theorem HMap.comp_mk (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ E) :
    HMap.comp (HMap.mk F) (HMap.mk G) = HMap.mk (F ⋙ G) := rfl

theorem HMap.comp_assoc {A' : Type u} [Category.{v} A'] (f : HMap A B) (g : HMap B E)
    (h : HMap E A') : HMap.comp (HMap.comp f g) h = HMap.comp f (HMap.comp g h) := by
  induction f using HMap.ind
  induction g using HMap.ind
  induction h using HMap.ind
  rfl

@[simp] theorem HMap.comp_id (f : HMap A B) : HMap.comp f (HMap.mk (𝟭 B)) = f := by
  induction f using HMap.ind; rfl

@[simp] theorem HMap.id_comp (f : HMap A B) : HMap.comp (HMap.mk (𝟭 A)) f = f := by
  induction f using HMap.ind; rfl

end HMap

/-! ## The matrix (wreath) monoid of a family of 1-types -/

section Wreath

variable {ι : Type w} (C : ι → Type u) [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)]

/-- A homotopy class of self-maps of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ`, in matrix form: a self-map `idx` of the
index set together with a homotopy class of maps `Cᵢ → C_{idx i}` for every `i`. -/
structure WreathHom where
  /-- The induced self-map of the index set. -/
  idx : ι → ι
  /-- The homotopy class of the `i`-th piece. -/
  cls : ∀ i, HMap (C i) (C (idx i))

variable {C}

theorem WreathHom.ext' {σ : ι → ι} {P Q : ∀ i, HMap (C i) (C (σ i))} (h : ∀ i, P i = Q i) :
    (⟨σ, P⟩ : WreathHom C) = ⟨σ, Q⟩ := by
  simpa using congrArg (WreathHom.mk σ) (funext h)

variable (C)

instance : Monoid (WreathHom C) where
  mul x y := ⟨fun i => x.idx (y.idx i), fun i => HMap.comp (y.cls i) (x.cls (y.idx i))⟩
  one := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.mk (𝟭 (C i))⟩
  mul_assoc x y z := WreathHom.ext' fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_assoc (z.cls i) (y.cls (z.idx i)) (x.cls (y.idx (z.idx i)))).symm
  one_mul x := WreathHom.ext' fun i => HMap.comp_id (x.cls i)
  mul_one x := WreathHom.ext' fun i => HMap.id_comp (x.cls i)

variable {C}

@[simp] theorem WreathHom.mul_idx (x y : WreathHom C) :
    (x * y).idx = fun i => x.idx (y.idx i) := rfl

@[simp] theorem WreathHom.mul_cls (x y : WreathHom C) (i : ι) :
    (x * y).cls i = HMap.comp (y.cls i) (x.cls (y.idx i)) := rfl

@[simp] theorem WreathHom.one_idx : (1 : WreathHom C).idx = fun i => i := rfl

@[simp] theorem WreathHom.one_cls (i : ι) : (1 : WreathHom C).cls i = HMap.mk (𝟭 (C i)) := rfl

/-- Every element of the matrix monoid is given by an honest family of functors. -/
@[elab_as_elim]
theorem WreathHom.ind {motive : WreathHom C → Prop}
    (h : ∀ (σ : ι → ι) (P : ∀ i, C i ⥤ C (σ i)), motive ⟨σ, fun i => HMap.mk (P i)⟩) :
    ∀ x, motive x := by
  rintro ⟨σ, P⟩
  have : (fun i => HMap.mk (Quotient.out (P i))) = P := funext fun i => HMap.mk_out (P i)
  simpa [this] using h σ fun i => Quotient.out (P i)

end Wreath

/-! ## Factoring a map out of a connected 1-type through a single component -/

section Factor

open FundamentalGroupPi0 (sigmaGroupoid autSigmaMulEquiv fst_eq_of_iso sigmaDesc)

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)]
  {A : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} A] {a : A}

/-- Applying the inclusion of a summand to a vertex-group element. -/
theorem autSigmaMulEquiv_hom (i : ι) (X : C i) (y : Aut X) :
    ((autSigmaMulEquiv i X) y).hom = (Sigma.incl i).map y.hom := rfl

/-- **A map out of a connected 1-type factors through a single component of the target.**
Up to homotopy, a functor from a connected groupoid to a disjoint union is the inclusion of
one summand precomposed with a functor into that summand. -/
theorem exists_factor (hA : ConnectedAt A a) (F : A ⥤ Σ i, C i) :
    ∃ (j : ι) (P : A ⥤ C j), Nonempty (F ≅ P ⋙ Sigma.incl j) := by
  refine ⟨(F.obj a).1, realize hA (F.obj a).2
    (((autSigmaMulEquiv (F.obj a).1 (F.obj a).2).symm).toMonoidHom.comp (F.mapAut a)), ?_⟩
  set j := (F.obj a).1 with hj
  set d := (F.obj a).2 with hd
  set ψ := ((autSigmaMulEquiv j d).symm).toMonoidHom.comp (F.mapAut a) with hψ
  rw [natIso_iff_conjugating_iso hA]
  refine ⟨Iso.refl _, fun x => ?_⟩
  have key : (Sigma.incl j).map ((ψ x).hom) = F.map x.hom := by
    have h1 : (autSigmaMulEquiv j d) (ψ x) = F.mapAut a x :=
      (autSigmaMulEquiv j d).apply_symm_apply _
    calc (Sigma.incl j).map ((ψ x).hom) = ((autSigmaMulEquiv j d) (ψ x)).hom :=
          (autSigmaMulEquiv_hom j d (ψ x)).symm
      _ = (F.mapAut a x).hom := by rw [h1]
      _ = F.map x.hom := rfl
  simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp, Functor.comp_map]
  rw [realize_map_aut, key]

/-- Two factorisations through summands use the same summand. -/
theorem index_eq_of_natIso_incl (a : A) {j k : ι} {P : A ⥤ C j} {Q : A ⥤ C k}
    (e : P ⋙ Sigma.incl j ≅ Q ⋙ Sigma.incl k) : j = k :=
  fst_eq_of_iso (e.app a)

/-- Two factorisations through the same summand are homotopic there. -/
theorem natIso_of_natIso_incl {j : ι} {P Q : A ⥤ C j}
    (e : P ⋙ Sigma.incl j ≅ Q ⋙ Sigma.incl j) : Nonempty (P ≅ Q) :=
  ⟨Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight (Sigma.incl j) e⟩

end Factor

/-! ## The matrix monoid computes all self-maps of a disjoint union -/

section Main

open FundamentalGroupPi0 (sigmaGroupoid fst_eq_of_iso sigmaDesc sigmaDesc_obj)

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)] {c : ∀ i, C i}

/-- The self-map of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` determined by a matrix of homotopy classes. -/
noncomputable def toHEnd (x : WreathHom C) : HEnd (Σ i, C i) :=
  HEnd.mk _ (sigmaDesc x.idx fun i => Quotient.out (x.cls i))

theorem toHEnd_mk (σ : ι → ι) (P : ∀ i, C i ⥤ C (σ i)) :
    toHEnd (⟨σ, fun i => HMap.mk (P i)⟩ : WreathHom C) = HEnd.mk _ (sigmaDesc σ P) := by
  refine HEnd.mk_eq_mk.2 ⟨Sigma.natIso fun i => ?_⟩
  have α : Quotient.out (HMap.mk (P i)) ≅ P i :=
    (HMap.mk_eq_mk.1 (HMap.mk_out (HMap.mk (P i)))).some
  exact (Sigma.inclDesc (fun i => Quotient.out (HMap.mk (P i)) ⋙ Sigma.incl (σ i)) i).trans
    ((Functor.isoWhiskerRight α (Sigma.incl (σ i))).trans
      (Sigma.inclDesc (fun i => P i ⋙ Sigma.incl (σ i)) i).symm)

/-- The composite of two assembled self-maps is the assembly of the matrix product. -/
theorem sigmaDesc_comp (σ τ : ι → ι) (P : ∀ i, C i ⥤ C (σ i)) (Q : ∀ i, C i ⥤ C (τ i)) :
    sigmaDesc τ Q ⋙ sigmaDesc σ P
      = sigmaDesc (fun i => σ (τ i)) fun i => Q i ⋙ P (τ i) := by
  refine CategoryTheory.Functor.ext (fun X => rfl) ?_
  rintro ⟨i, X⟩ ⟨_, Y⟩ ⟨f⟩
  simp [FundamentalGroupPi0.sigmaDesc_map]

theorem toHEnd_one : toHEnd (1 : WreathHom C) = 1 := by
  have h := toHEnd_mk (C := C) (fun i => i) fun i => 𝟭 (C i)
  rw [show (1 : WreathHom C) = ⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.mk (𝟭 (C i))⟩ from rfl, h]
  refine HEnd.mk_eq_mk.2 ⟨Sigma.natIso fun i => ?_⟩
  exact (Sigma.inclDesc _ i).trans (Functor.leftUnitor _)

theorem toHEnd_mul (x y : WreathHom C) : toHEnd (x * y) = toHEnd x * toHEnd y := by
  induction x using WreathHom.ind with
  | _ σ P =>
    induction y using WreathHom.ind with
    | _ τ Q =>
      have hprod : (⟨σ, fun i => HMap.mk (P i)⟩ : WreathHom C)
            * ⟨τ, fun i => HMap.mk (Q i)⟩
            = ⟨fun i => σ (τ i), fun i => HMap.mk (Q i ⋙ P (τ i))⟩ := rfl
      rw [hprod, toHEnd_mk, toHEnd_mk, toHEnd_mk, HEnd.mk_mul, sigmaDesc_comp]

/-- The matrix monoid maps to homotopy classes of self-maps of the disjoint union. -/
noncomputable def toHEndHom : WreathHom C →* HEnd (Σ i, C i) where
  toFun := toHEnd
  map_one' := toHEnd_one
  map_mul' := toHEnd_mul

@[simp] theorem toHEndHom_apply (x : WreathHom C) : toHEndHom x = toHEnd x := rfl

theorem toHEnd_injective (c : ∀ i, C i) :
    Function.Injective (toHEnd (C := C)) := by
  intro x y hxy
  induction x using WreathHom.ind with
  | _ σ P =>
    induction y using WreathHom.ind with
    | _ τ Q =>
      rw [toHEnd_mk, toHEnd_mk] at hxy
      obtain ⟨e⟩ := HEnd.mk_eq_mk.1 hxy
      have epieces : ∀ i, P i ⋙ Sigma.incl (σ i) ≅ Q i ⋙ Sigma.incl (τ i) := fun i =>
        ((Sigma.inclDesc _ i).symm.trans (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Sigma.incl i) e)).trans
          (Sigma.inclDesc _ i)
      have hst : σ = τ := funext fun i => index_eq_of_natIso_incl (c i) (epieces i)
      subst hst
      exact WreathHom.ext' fun i =>
        HMap.mk_eq_mk.2 (natIso_of_natIso_incl (epieces i))

theorem toHEnd_surjective (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    Function.Surjective (toHEnd (C := C)) := by
  intro q
  induction q using HEnd.ind with
  | _ F =>
    choose σ P hP using fun i => exists_factor (hC i) (Sigma.incl i ⋙ F)
    refine ⟨⟨σ, fun i => HMap.mk (P i)⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [toHEnd_mk]
    exact HEnd.mk_eq_mk.2 ⟨(Sigma.descUniq _ F fun i => (hP i).some).symm⟩

/-- **All self-maps of a disjoint union of connected 1-types.**  The monoid of homotopy
classes of self-maps of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` is the matrix monoid: a self-map `σ` of the set of
components together with, for each `i`, a homotopy class of maps `Cᵢ → C_{σ i}`. -/
noncomputable def wreathMulEquivHEndSigma (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    WreathHom C ≃* HEnd (Σ i, C i) :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective toHEndHom ⟨toHEnd_injective c, toHEnd_surjective hC⟩

@[simp] theorem wreathMulEquivHEndSigma_apply (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i))
    (x : WreathHom C) : wreathMulEquivHEndSigma hC x = toHEnd x := rfl

/-- **The matrix description of homotopy classes of self-maps**, stated as an isomorphism
out of the monoid of self-maps of the disjoint union. -/
noncomputable def hEndSigmaMulEquivWreath (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    HEnd (Σ i, C i) ≃* WreathHom C := (wreathMulEquivHEndSigma hC).symm

end Main

/-! ## The permutation of the components induced by a self-equivalence -/

section Units

open FundamentalGroupPi0 (sigmaGroupoid fst_eq_of_iso sigmaDesc)

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)] {c : ∀ i, C i}

theorem WreathHom.cls_inj {σ : ι → ι} {P Q : ∀ i, HMap (C i) (C (σ i))}
    (h : (⟨σ, P⟩ : WreathHom C) = ⟨σ, Q⟩) : P = Q := by simpa using h

/-- Composition of homotopy classes of self-maps is the monoid product of `HEnd`,
with the arguments in the other order. -/
theorem HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] (p q : HEnd A) :
    HMap.comp q p = p * q := by
  induction p using HEnd.ind
  induction q using HEnd.ind
  rfl

/-- The permutation of the set of components induced by an invertible matrix. -/
def unitsPerm (u : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : Equiv.Perm ι where
  toFun := u.val.idx
  invFun := u.inv.idx
  left_inv i := congrFun (congrArg WreathHom.idx u.inv_val) i
  right_inv i := congrFun (congrArg WreathHom.idx u.val_inv) i

@[simp] theorem unitsPerm_apply (u : (WreathHom C)ˣ) (i : ι) : unitsPerm u i = u.val.idx i :=
  rfl

/-- **The action on the set of components.**  A homotopy self-equivalence of a disjoint
union permutes the components. -/
def wreathHomUnitsToPerm : (WreathHom C)ˣ →* Equiv.Perm ι where
  toFun := unitsPerm
  map_one' := Equiv.ext fun _ => rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := Equiv.ext fun _ => rfl

@[simp] theorem wreathHomUnitsToPerm_apply (u : (WreathHom C)ˣ) (i : ι) :
    wreathHomUnitsToPerm u i = u.val.idx i := rfl

/-- The diagonal embedding of the self-maps of the individual components. -/
def piHEndToWreath : (∀ i, HEnd (C i)) →* WreathHom C where
  toFun f := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => f i⟩
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' f g := WreathHom.ext' fun i => (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (f i) (g i)).symm

@[simp] theorem piHEndToWreath_idx (f : ∀ i, HEnd (C i)) :
    (piHEndToWreath f).idx = fun i => i := rfl

@[simp] theorem piHEndToWreath_cls (f : ∀ i, HEnd (C i)) (i : ι) :
    (piHEndToWreath f).cls i = f i := rfl

theorem piHEndToWreath_injective : Function.Injective (piHEndToWreath (C := C)) :=
  fun _ _ h => WreathHom.cls_inj h

/-- Diagonal matrices are exactly those whose permutation of the components is trivial. -/
theorem unitsPerm_eq_one_iff (u : (WreathHom C)ˣ) :
    unitsPerm u = 1 ↔ u.val.idx = fun i => i :=
  ⟨fun h => funext fun i => congrFun (congrArg (fun e : Equiv.Perm ι => (e : ι → ι)) h) i,
    fun h => Equiv.ext fun i => congrFun h i⟩

/-- A family of homotopy self-equivalences of the components, viewed as a homotopy
self-equivalence of the disjoint union fixing each component. -/
def diagUnitsHom (f : ∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) : (WreathHom C)ˣ where
  val := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => (f i).val⟩
  inv := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => (f i).inv⟩
  val_inv := WreathHom.ext' fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (f i).val (f i).inv).trans (f i).val_inv
  inv_val := WreathHom.ext' fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (f i).inv (f i).val).trans (f i).inv_val

@[simp] theorem diagUnitsHom_val_cls (f : ∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) (i : ι) :
    ((diagUnitsHom f : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : WreathHom C).cls i = (f i : HEnd (C i)) := rfl

@[simp] theorem diagUnitsHom_val_idx (f : ∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) :
    ((diagUnitsHom f : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : WreathHom C).idx = fun i => i := rfl

/-- The diagonal embedding is a group homomorphism. -/
def diagUnitsMonoidHom : (∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) →* (WreathHom C)ˣ where
  toFun := diagUnitsHom
  map_one' := Units.ext (WreathHom.ext' fun _ => rfl)
  map_mul' f g := Units.ext (WreathHom.ext' fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (f i : HEnd (C i)) (g i : HEnd (C i))).symm)

/-- The diagonal embedding lands in the kernel of the action on the components. -/
def diagUnits : (∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) →* (wreathHomUnitsToPerm (C := C)).ker :=
  MonoidHom.codRestrict diagUnitsMonoidHom _ fun _ =>
    MonoidHom.mem_ker.2 ((unitsPerm_eq_one_iff _).2 rfl)

theorem diagUnits_injective : Function.Injective (diagUnits (C := C)) := by
  intro f g h
  have h1 : ((diagUnitsHom f : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : WreathHom C)
      = ((diagUnitsHom g : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : WreathHom C) :=
    congrArg (fun u : (wreathHomUnitsToPerm (C := C)).ker => ((u : (WreathHom C)ˣ) : WreathHom C)) h
  have h2 := WreathHom.cls_inj h1
  exact funext fun i => Units.ext (congrFun h2 i)

theorem diagUnits_surjective : Function.Surjective (diagUnits (C := C)) := by
  rintro ⟨u, hu⟩
  have hidx : u.val.idx = fun i => i := (unitsPerm_eq_one_iff u).1 (MonoidHom.mem_ker.1 hu)
  have hidx' : u.inv.idx = fun i => i := by
    have h := congrArg WreathHom.idx u.val_inv
    simp only [WreathHom.mul_idx, WreathHom.one_idx, hidx] at h
    exact h
  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy, hyx⟩ := u
  simp only at hidx hidx'
  obtain ⟨σ, P⟩ := x
  obtain ⟨τ, Q⟩ := y
  simp only at hidx hidx'
  subst hidx
  subst hidx'
  have key : (⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.comp (Q i) (P i)⟩ : WreathHom C)
      = ⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.mk (𝟭 (C i))⟩ := hxy
  have key' : (⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.comp (P i) (Q i)⟩ : WreathHom C)
      = ⟨fun i => i, fun i => HMap.mk (𝟭 (C i))⟩ := hyx
  let P' : ∀ i, HEnd (C i) := fun i => P i
  let Q' : ∀ i, HEnd (C i) := fun i => Q i
  have hPQ : ∀ i, P' i * Q' i = 1 := fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (P' i) (Q' i)).symm.trans (congrFun (WreathHom.cls_inj key) i)
  have hQP : ∀ i, Q' i * P' i = 1 := fun i =>
    (HMap.comp_eq_hEnd_mul (Q' i) (P' i)).symm.trans (congrFun (WreathHom.cls_inj key') i)
  exact ⟨fun i => ⟨P' i, Q' i, hPQ i, hQP i⟩, rfl⟩

/-- **The kernel of the action on components.**  A homotopy self-equivalence of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ`
fixing every component is exactly a family of homotopy self-equivalences of the
components. -/
noncomputable def diagUnitsMulEquivKer :
    (∀ i, (HEnd (C i))ˣ) ≃* (wreathHomUnitsToPerm (C := C)).ker :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective diagUnits ⟨diagUnits_injective, diagUnits_surjective⟩

/-- **The kernel of the action on components is `∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ)`.** -/
noncomputable def kerMulEquivPiOut (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    (wreathHomUnitsToPerm (C := C)).ker ≃* ∀ i, OutAut (Aut (c i)) :=
  diagUnitsMulEquivKer.symm.trans
    (MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i => (outAut_mulEquiv_hEnd_units (hC i)).symm)

end Units

/-! ## The homotopy self-equivalence group of a disjoint union -/

section HAut

open FundamentalGroupPi0 (sigmaGroupoid fst_eq_of_iso sigmaDesc sigmaDesc_full
  sigmaDesc_faithful sigmaDesc_essSurj indexEquivOfEquivalence aut_mulEquiv_of_equivalence)

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)] {c : ∀ i, C i}

/-- The index map of a matrix is read off from any representative of the corresponding
homotopy class of self-maps of the disjoint union. -/
theorem idx_eq_of_toHEnd (c : ∀ i, C i) (x : WreathHom C) (F : (Σ i, C i) ⥤ Σ i, C i)
    (h : toHEnd x = HEnd.mk _ F) (i : ι) : x.idx i = (F.obj ⟨i, c i⟩).1 := by
  induction x using WreathHom.ind with
  | _ σ P =>
    rw [toHEnd_mk] at h
    obtain ⟨e⟩ := HEnd.mk_eq_mk.1 h
    exact fst_eq_of_iso (e.app ⟨i, c i⟩)

/-- The matrix description of the homotopy self-equivalence group. -/
noncomputable def unitsWreathEquiv (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ ≃* (WreathHom C)ˣ :=
  Units.mapEquiv (hEndSigmaMulEquivWreath hC)

/-- **The action of the homotopy self-equivalence group of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` on its set of
components.** -/
noncomputable def hAutSigmaToPerm (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ →* Equiv.Perm ι :=
  wreathHomUnitsToPerm.comp (unitsWreathEquiv hC).toMonoidHom

/-- The permutation induced by a self-equivalence sends the component `i` to the component
containing the image of the basepoint of `Cᵢ`. -/
theorem hAutSigmaToPerm_apply (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i))
    (u : (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ) (F : (Σ i, C i) ⥤ Σ i, C i)
    (hF : (u : HEnd (Σ i, C i)) = HEnd.mk _ F) (i : ι) :
    hAutSigmaToPerm hC u i = (F.obj ⟨i, c i⟩).1 := by
  refine idx_eq_of_toHEnd c _ F ?_ i
  show (wreathMulEquivHEndSigma hC) ((hEndSigmaMulEquivWreath hC) (u : HEnd (Σ i, C i)))
      = HEnd.mk _ F
  rw [← hF]
  exact (wreathMulEquivHEndSigma hC).apply_symm_apply _

/-- Every homotopy class of self-maps has a representative functor. -/
theorem exists_rep_hEnd {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (q : HEnd D) :
    ∃ F : D ⥤ D, q = HEnd.mk D F :=
  (Quotient.exists_rep q).imp fun _ hF => hF.symm

/-- **The image of the action on components.**  A permutation of the set of components is
induced by a homotopy self-equivalence exactly when it preserves the homotopy type of every
component. -/
theorem exists_hAut_perm_iff (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
    (∃ u : (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ, hAutSigmaToPerm hC u = σ) ↔ ∀ i, Nonempty (C i ≌ C (σ i)) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, rfl⟩ i
    obtain ⟨F, hF⟩ := exists_rep_hEnd (u : HEnd (Σ i, C i))
    haveI hFe : F.IsEquivalence := by
      rw [← isUnit_hEnd_mk_iff, ← hF]
      exact u.isUnit
    have hidx : (F.obj ⟨i, c i⟩).1 = hAutSigmaToPerm hC u i :=
      (hAutSigmaToPerm_apply hC u F hF i).symm
    obtain ⟨w⟩ := aut_mulEquiv_of_equivalence c c hC hC F.asEquivalence i
    have w' : Aut (c i) ≃* Aut (c (hAutSigmaToPerm hC u i)) := hidx ▸ w
    exact FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant.connectedGroupoids_equivalent_of_aut_mulEquiv
      (c i) (c (hAutSigmaToPerm hC u i)) (hC i) (hC _) w'
  · intro h
    have E : ∀ i, C i ≌ C (σ i) := fun i => (h i).some
    haveI : ∀ i, (E i).functor.Full := fun i => inferInstance
    haveI : ∀ i, (E i).functor.Faithful := fun i => inferInstance
    haveI : ∀ i, (E i).functor.EssSurj := fun i => inferInstance
    haveI := sigmaDesc_full σ.injective (fun i => (E i).functor) fun i => inferInstance
    haveI := sigmaDesc_faithful (fun i => (E i).functor) fun i => inferInstance
    haveI := sigmaDesc_essSurj σ.surjective (fun i => (E i).functor) fun i => inferInstance
    have hFe : (sigmaDesc (σ : ι → ι) fun i => (E i).functor).IsEquivalence :=
      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    have hunit : IsUnit (HEnd.mk (Σ i, C i) (sigmaDesc (σ : ι → ι) fun i => (E i).functor)) :=
      (isUnit_hEnd_mk_iff _).2 hFe
    refine ⟨hunit.unit, Equiv.ext fun i => ?_⟩
    rw [hAutSigmaToPerm_apply hC hunit.unit _ hunit.unit_spec.symm i]
    rfl

theorem map_ker_hAutSigmaToPerm (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    Subgroup.map (unitsWreathEquiv hC).toMonoidHom (hAutSigmaToPerm hC).ker
      = (wreathHomUnitsToPerm (C := C)).ker := by
  ext u
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
    exact MonoidHom.mem_ker.1 hv
  · intro hu
    refine ⟨(unitsWreathEquiv hC).symm u, MonoidHom.mem_ker.2 ?_,
      (unitsWreathEquiv hC).apply_symm_apply u⟩
    show wreathHomUnitsToPerm ((unitsWreathEquiv hC) ((unitsWreathEquiv hC).symm u)) = 1
    rw [(unitsWreathEquiv hC).apply_symm_apply u]
    exact MonoidHom.mem_ker.1 hu

/-- **Exactness at `hAut`.**  The homotopy self-equivalences of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` inducing the
identity permutation of the components are exactly `∏ᵢ Out(π₁ Cᵢ)`. -/
noncomputable def kerHAutSigmaToPermMulEquivPiOut (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    (hAutSigmaToPerm hC).ker ≃* ∀ i, OutAut (Aut (c i)) :=
  (((unitsWreathEquiv hC).subgroupMap (hAutSigmaToPerm hC).ker).trans
    (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (map_ker_hAutSigmaToPerm hC))).trans (kerMulEquivPiOut hC)

/-! ## Rigid families: no two components of the same homotopy type -/

/-- **A disjoint union of pairwise inequivalent connected 1-types.**  If no two distinct
components are homotopy equivalent, no self-equivalence can move a component, so the whole
action on `π₀` is trivial. -/
theorem hAutSigmaToPerm_eq_one_of_pairwise (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i))
    (hne : ∀ i j : ι, Nonempty (C i ≌ C j) → i = j) (u : (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ) :
    hAutSigmaToPerm hC u = 1 := by
  have h := (exists_hAut_perm_iff hC (hAutSigmaToPerm hC u)).1 ⟨u, rfl⟩
  exact Equiv.ext fun i => (hne i _ (h i)).symm

/-- **The homotopy self-equivalence group of a disjoint union of pairwise inequivalent
`K(Gᵢ,1)`s is `∏ᵢ Out(Gᵢ)`** — no relabelling of components is possible. -/
noncomputable def hAutMulEquivPiOut_of_pairwise (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i))
    (hne : ∀ i j : ι, Nonempty (C i ≌ C j) → i = j) :
    (HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ ≃* ∀ i, OutAut (Aut (c i)) :=
  Subgroup.topEquiv.symm.trans
    ((MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (show (⊤ : Subgroup ((HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ)) = (hAutSigmaToPerm hC).ker by
        ext u
        simpa [MonoidHom.mem_ker] using hAutSigmaToPerm_eq_one_of_pairwise hC hne u)).trans
      (kerHAutSigmaToPermMulEquivPiOut hC))

/-- The number of homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences of a disjoint union of
finitely many pairwise inequivalent `K(Gᵢ,1)`s is `∏ᵢ |Out(Gᵢ)|`. -/
theorem card_hAut_of_pairwise [Fintype ι] (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i))
    (hne : ∀ i j : ι, Nonempty (C i ≌ C j) → i = j) :
    Nat.card ((HEnd (Σ i, C i))ˣ) = ∏ i, Nat.card (OutAut (Aut (c i))) := by
  rw [Nat.card_congr (hAutMulEquivPiOut_of_pairwise hC hne).toEquiv, Nat.card_pi]

end HAut

/-! ## The self-homotopies of the identity -/

section AutId

open FundamentalGroupPi0 (sigmaGroupoid)

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)] {c : ∀ i, C i}

/-- The self-homotopy of the identity of the `i`-th component induced by a self-homotopy of
the identity of the disjoint union. -/
noncomputable def restrictAutIdSigma (α : Aut (𝟭 (Σ i, C i))) (i : ι) : Aut (𝟭 (C i)) :=
  Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight (Sigma.incl i) (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Sigma.incl i) α)

@[simp] theorem restrictAutIdSigma_hom_app (α : Aut (𝟭 (Σ i, C i))) (i : ι) (X : C i) :
    (restrictAutIdSigma α i).hom.app X = (Sigma.incl i).preimage (α.hom.app ⟨i, X⟩) := rfl

/-- A family of self-homotopies of the identities of the components assembles into a
self-homotopy of the identity of the disjoint union. -/
def assembleAutIdSigma (β : ∀ i, Aut (𝟭 (C i))) : Aut (𝟭 (Σ i, C i)) :=
  Sigma.natIso fun i => Functor.isoWhiskerRight (β i) (Sigma.incl i)

@[simp] theorem assembleAutIdSigma_hom_app (β : ∀ i, Aut (𝟭 (C i))) (i : ι) (X : C i) :
    (assembleAutIdSigma β).hom.app ⟨i, X⟩ = (Sigma.incl i).map ((β i).hom.app X) := rfl

/-- **The self-homotopies of the identity of `⊔ᵢ Cᵢ` are families of self-homotopies of the
identities of the components.** -/
noncomputable def autIdSigmaMulEquivPi : Aut (𝟭 (Σ i, C i)) ≃* ∀ i, Aut (𝟭 (C i)) where
  toFun := restrictAutIdSigma
  invFun := assembleAutIdSigma
  left_inv α := by
    apply Iso.ext
    ext ⟨i, X⟩
    exact (Sigma.incl i).map_preimage (α.hom.app ⟨i, X⟩)
  right_inv β := by
    funext i
    apply Iso.ext
    ext X
    exact (Sigma.incl i).preimage_map ((β i).hom.app X)
  map_mul' α γ := by
    funext i
    apply Iso.ext
    ext X
    apply (Sigma.incl i).map_injective
    simp [Aut.Aut_mul_def]

/-- **The `π₁` of the automorphism 2-group of an arbitrary 1-type is `∏ᵢ Z(π₁ Cᵢ)`.**
Together with `kerHAutSigmaToPermMulEquivPiOut` and `exists_hAut_perm_iff` (which compute
`π₀`) this determines the whole automorphism 2-group of a disjoint union of arbitrary
connected 1-types. -/
noncomputable def autIdSigmaMulEquivPiCenter (hC : ∀ i, ConnectedAt (C i) (c i)) :
    Aut (𝟭 (Σ i, C i)) ≃* ∀ i, Subgroup.center (Aut (c i)) :=
  autIdSigmaMulEquivPi.trans (MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i => autId_mulEquiv_center (hC i))

end AutId

end FundamentalGroupHetero

-- ===== FILE: Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupMapsClassification.lean =====
/-
# The complete classification of maps between arbitrary 1-types

This file assembles the two remaining pieces of the classification of maps of homotopy
1-types (groupoids), with **no connectedness assumptions on either side**:

* `mapsFromSigmaEquiv` : homotopy classes of maps out of a disjoint union are families of
  homotopy classes of maps out of the summands,
  `[⊔ᵢ Cᵢ, D] ≃ ∏ᵢ [Cᵢ, D]`;
* `totalEquiv` : homotopy classes of maps out of a *connected* 1-type are a choice of
  connected component of the target together with a conjugacy class of homomorphisms into
  the fundamental group of that component (the total form of
  `FundamentalGroupMapsDisc.fibreEquiv`);
* `mapsClassification` : combining the two,

  `[⊔ᵢ K(Gᵢ,1), D] ≃ ∏ᵢ (Σ q ∈ π₀ D, Hom(Gᵢ, π₁(D,q)) / conjugation)`.

Since every 1-type is the disjoint union of its connected components (proved in
`Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupPi0Decomposition.lean`), this is the complete answer to
"what are the maps between two homotopy 1-types, up to homotopy?", purely in terms of
`π₀` and the fundamental groups.
-/
import Mathlib
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupMapsDisconnectedTarget
import Catalog.Bridges.FundamentalGroupPi0Gluing

open CategoryTheory
open FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant (ConnectedAt)
open FundamentalGroupK1
open FundamentalGroupK1Deep (Components isoSetoid)
open FundamentalGroupMapsDisc (toComponent fibreEquiv)

namespace FundamentalGroupMapsAll

universe w v u u'

/-! ## Maps out of a disjoint union -/

section Coproduct

variable {ι : Type w} {C : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Groupoid.{v} (C i)]
  {D : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} D]

/-- Restriction of a homotopy class of maps out of a coproduct to the summands. -/
def restrictClasses :
    Quotient (natIsoSetoid (Σ i, C i) D) → ∀ i, Quotient (natIsoSetoid (C i) D) :=
  Quotient.lift (fun F i => Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (C i) D) (Sigma.incl i ⋙ F))
    (by
      rintro F G ⟨e⟩
      funext i
      exact Quotient.sound ⟨Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Sigma.incl i) e⟩)

/-- Assembling a family of homotopy classes into a homotopy class of maps out of the
coproduct. -/
noncomputable def assembleClasses :
    (∀ i, Quotient (natIsoSetoid (C i) D)) → Quotient (natIsoSetoid (Σ i, C i) D) :=
  fun f => Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (Σ i, C i) D) (Sigma.desc fun i => Quotient.out (f i))

/-- **Maps out of a disjoint union of 1-types are families of maps out of the pieces.** -/
noncomputable def mapsFromSigmaEquiv :
    Quotient (natIsoSetoid (Σ i, C i) D) ≃ ∀ i, Quotient (natIsoSetoid (C i) D) where
  toFun := restrictClasses
  invFun := assembleClasses
  left_inv q := by
    induction q using Quotient.ind with
    | _ F =>
      refine Quotient.sound ⟨(Sigma.descUniq _ F fun i => ?_).symm⟩
      have hrel : (natIsoSetoid (C i) D).r
          (Quotient.out (Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (C i) D) (Sigma.incl i ⋙ F)))
          (Sigma.incl i ⋙ F) :=
        Quotient.exact (Quotient.out_eq _)
      exact hrel.some.symm
  right_inv f := by
    funext i
    show Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (C i) D)
        (Sigma.incl i ⋙ Sigma.desc fun j => Quotient.out (f j)) = f i
    have h1 : Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (C i) D)
          (Sigma.incl i ⋙ Sigma.desc fun j => Quotient.out (f j))
        = Quotient.mk (natIsoSetoid (C i) D) (Quotient.out (f i)) :=
      Quotient.sound (Nonempty.intro (Sigma.inclDesc _ i))
    rw [h1, Quotient.out_eq]

end Coproduct

/-! ## Maps out of a connected 1-type, in total form -/

section Connected

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v} D]

/-- **Maps out of a `K(G,1)` into an arbitrary 1-type**: a homotopy class is exactly a
component `q` of the target together with a conjugacy class of homomorphisms
