# Future directions

This line of work studies **when the fundamental group is a complete invariant**, in the algebraic model where a homotopy 1-type is a groupoid and a $K(G,1)$ is a connected groupoid with vertex group $G$. Previous cycles classified the objects (a connected 1-type is determined by $\pi_1$), the maps ($[K(G,1), K(H,1)] \simeq \mathrm{Hom}(G,H)/\mathrm{conj}$), and the automorphism 2-group of a connected 1-type ($\pi_0 = \mathrm{Out}\,G$, $\pi_1 = Z(G)$).

Later cycles closed the largest structural gap that remained — the description of $\mathrm{hAut}$ for a **disconnected** 1-type — and supplied the first **nonabelian** examples.

The present cycle removes the last hypothesis from that description: the components of the disjoint union no longer have to be copies of a single $K(G,1)$. For a completely arbitrary 1-type the monoid of homotopy classes of self-maps is a matrix monoid, and

$$1 \to \prod_i \mathrm{Out}(\pi_1 C_i) \to \mathrm{hAut}\Bigl(\bigsqcup_i C_i\Bigr) \to \mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0) \to 1$$

is exact, with $\mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0)$ the permutations of the components preserving their homotopy type; the self-homotopies of the identity are $\prod_i Z(\pi_1 C_i)$.

## What has been established

### Earlier cycles

* The monoid $\mathrm{hEnd}(C)$ of homotopy classes of self-maps and the monoid $\mathrm{ConjEnd}(G)$ of conjugacy classes of endomorphisms are isomorphic for a connected $C$.
* A homotopy class is invertible if and only if it is represented by an equivalence.
* **$\mathrm{hAut}(K(G,1)) \cong \mathrm{Out}\,G$**, and the self-homotopies of the identity form $Z(G)$.
* The abelian case, a rigidity criterion, one-object models, and the circle: $\mathrm{hEnd}(S^1) \cong (\mathbb{Z},\cdot)$, degree a complete invariant, equivalences $\iff$ degree $\pm 1$.
* $\#\mathrm{hAut}(K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)) = \varphi(n)$; $\mathrm{hAut}(K(\mathbb{Z}^n,1)) \cong \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$; for a totally disconnected 1-type, $\mathrm{hAut} \cong \mathrm{Sym}(\pi_0)$; the classification of maps of arbitrary 1-types in terms of $\pi_0$ and the vertex groups; and the action $\mathrm{hAut}(C) \to \mathrm{Sym}(\pi_0 C)$ together with the injective assembly of self-maps of the pieces of a disjoint union.

### Earlier cycles: the constant-family wreath product and nonabelian examples

* The wreath monoid $(\iota \to M) \times \mathrm{End}(\iota)$ with $(P,\sigma)(Q,\tau) = (i \mapsto P(\tau i)\, Q(i),\; \sigma \circ \tau)$.
* For a connected $D$, $[\bigsqcup_\iota D, \bigsqcup_\iota D]$ is the wreath monoid on $[D,D]$ — a homotopy class of self-maps of the disjoint union is exactly an index map $\sigma : \iota \to \iota$ together with a homotopy class of maps $D \to D$ for each copy. This classifies *all* self-maps, not only the equivalences.
* The units of the wreath monoid form the semidirect product $(\iota \to M^\times) \rtimes \mathrm{Sym}(\iota)$, whence $\mathrm{hAut}(\bigsqcup_\iota K(G,1)) \cong \mathrm{Out}(G) \wr \mathrm{Sym}(\iota)$, of order $|\mathrm{Out}\,G|^n \cdot n!$ for $n$ copies, with the extension over $\mathrm{Sym}(\iota)$ split.
* Nonabelian examples: every automorphism of $S_3$ is inner, so $K(S_3,1)$ is homotopy rigid; the Klein four group gives the first $K(G,1)$ with nonabelian homotopy self-equivalence group, of order 6.

## Open problems and next steps

1. **Non-splitting.** Determine exactly when the extension splits. It splits for a constant family; construct families where it does not, and describe the classifying cohomology class.
2. **Infinite index sets.** For an infinite set of components, $\mathrm{Sym}'(\pi_0)$ carries a natural topology; investigate the resulting topological group structure on $\mathrm{hAut}$.
3. **More outer automorphism groups.** The theorems are only as useful as the $\mathrm{Out}$ computations available. Extend the library to free groups ($\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$), surface groups (mapping class groups, via Dehn–Nielsen–Baer), and finitely generated abelian groups in general.
4. **Beyond 1-types.** Move to 2-types, whose invariants are $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$ as a $\pi_1$-module, and a $k$-invariant in $H^3(\pi_1;\pi_2)$, and describe $\mathrm{hAut}$ as an extension involving the automorphisms of the $k$-invariant.
5. **Equivariant and fibrewise versions.** Replace groupoids by groupoids over a fixed base, or by $G$-groupoids, and identify the corresponding symmetry groups.
6. **Effective computation.** Turn the matrix normal form into a decision procedure for homotopy of self-maps of finite 1-types, and analyse its complexity relative to the group isomorphism problem.
